sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneḥ saubalasya ca duḥśāsanacaturthānām idam āsīd viceṣṭitam
english: This was the scheming of Duryodhana, Karṇa, Śakuni the son of Subala, and Duḥśāsana as the fourth.

sanskrit: purāyam asmān gṛhṇāti kṣiprakārī janārdanaḥ sahito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa rājñā śāṃtanavena ca
english: "Before this swift-acting Janārdana seizes us, together with King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the son of Shantanu —

sanskrit: vayam eva hṛṣīkeśaṃ nigṛhṇīma balād iva prasahya puruṣavyāghram indro vairocaniṃ yathā
english: "Let us ourselves restrain Hrishikesha by force, overpowering that tiger among men, as Indra once subdued Vairocana."

sanskrit: śrutvā gṛhītaṃ vārṣṇeyaṃ pāṇḍavā hatacetasaḥ nirutsāhā bhaviṣyanti bhagnadaṃṣṭrā ivoragāḥ
english: "Hearing that the scion of Vṛṣṇi has been seized, the Pāṇḍavas will lose heart and become dispirited, like serpents with broken fangs."

sanskrit: ayaṃ hy eṣāṃ mahābāhuḥ sarveṣāṃ śarma varma ca asmin gṛhīte varade ṛṣabhe sarvasātvatām nirudyamā bhaviṣyanti pāṇḍavāḥ somakaiḥ saha
english: "For this mighty-armed one is the refuge and armour of them all. Once this boon-granting bull of all the Sātvatas is seized, the Pāṇḍavas together with the Somakas will become devoid of effort."

sanskrit: tasmād vayam ihaivainaṃ keśavaṃ kṣiprakāriṇam krośato dhṛtarāṣṭrasya baddhvā yotsyāmahe ripūn
english: "Therefore, right here, let us bind this swift-acting Keśava even as Dhṛtarāṣṭra cries out, and then we shall fight our enemies."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ pāpam abhiprāyaṃ pāpānāṃ duṣṭacetasām iṅgitajñaḥ kaviḥ kṣipram anvabudhyata sātyakiḥ
english: The wise Sātyaki, skilled in reading signs, quickly perceived the wicked intention of those wicked, corrupt-minded men.

sanskrit: tadartham abhiniṣkramya hārdikyena sahāsthitaḥ abravīt kṛtavarmāṇaṃ kṣipraṃ yojaya vāhinīm
english: Going out for that purpose and standing together with Hārdikya, he said to Kṛtavarman: "Quickly marshal the troops."

sanskrit: vyūḍhānīkaḥ sabhādvāram upatiṣṭhasva daṃśitaḥ yāvad ākhyāmy ahaṃ caitat kṛṣṇāyākliṣṭakarmaṇe
english: "Stand at the door of the assembly hall, armoured, with the forces arrayed, until I report this to Kṛṣṇa, the tireless in action."

sanskrit: sa praviśya sabhāṃ vīraḥ siṃho giriguhām iva ācaṣṭa tam abhiprāyaṃ keśavāya mahātmane
english: That hero, entering the assembly hall like a lion entering a mountain cave, disclosed that intention to the great-souled Keśava.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ tataś caiva viduraṃ cānvabhāṣata teṣām etam abhiprāyam ācacakṣe smayann iva
english: Then he also spoke to Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Vidura, and with a slight smile, revealed to them that intention of theirs.

sanskrit: dharmād apetam arthāc ca karma sādhuvigarhitam mandāḥ kartum ihecchanti na cāvāpyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "Fools desire here to commit an act that is contrary to righteousness and self-interest, censured by the good, and moreover one that can by no means be accomplished."

sanskrit: purā vikurvate mūḍhāḥ pāpātmānaḥ samāgatāḥ dharṣitāḥ kāmamanyubhyāṃ krodhalobhavaśānugāḥ
english: "These assembled fools, evil-souled, goaded by desire and anger, swayed by wrath and greed, are about to misbehave."

sanskrit: imaṃ hi puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ jighṛkṣanty alpacetasaḥ paṭenāgniṃ prajvalitaṃ yathā bālā yathā jaḍāḥ
english: "These feeble-minded ones wish to seize this lotus-eyed one, as children or fools might try to catch blazing fire in a cloth."

sanskrit: sātyakes tad vacaḥ śrutvā viduro dīrghadarśivān dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahābāhum abravīt kurusaṃsadi
english: Having heard those words of Sātyaki, the far-sighted Vidura addressed the mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the assembly of the Kurus.

sanskrit: rājan parītakālās te putrāḥ sarve paraṃtapa ayaśasyam aśakyaṃ ca karma kartuṃ samudyatāḥ
english: "O king, O afflicterof foes, all your sons, whose time has come, are bent on committing a deed that is both inglorious and impossible."

sanskrit: imaṃ hi puṇḍarīkākṣam abhibhūya prasahya ca nigrahītuṃ kilecchanti sahitā vāsavānujam
english: "For together they desire to overpower and forcibly restrain this lotus-eyed one, the younger brother of Vāsava."

sanskrit: imaṃ puruṣaśārdūlam apradhṛṣyaṃ durāsadam āsādya na bhaviṣyanti pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: "Attacking this tiger among men, this one who is unconquerable and unapproachable, they shall perish like moths rushing into fire."

sanskrit: ayam icchan hi tān sarvān yatamānāñ janārdanaḥ siṃho mṛgān iva kruddho gamayed yamasādanam
english: "For if Janārdana wished, he could send all of them striving against him to the abode of Yama, like an enraged lion dispatching deer."

sanskrit: na tv ayaṃ ninditaṃ karma kuryāt kṛṣṇaḥ kathaṃ cana na ca dharmād apakrāmed acyutaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: "But this Kṛṣṇa, the Immovable, the Foremost of Persons, would by no means commit a censured act, nor would he deviate from righteousness."

sanskrit: vidureṇaivam ukte tu keśavo vākyam abravīt dhṛtarāṣṭram abhiprekṣya suhṛdāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ mithaḥ
english: When Vidura had spoken thus, Keśava addressed a speech to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, while friends listened to one another.

sanskrit: rājann ete yadi kruddhā māṃ nigṛhṇīyur ojasā ete vā mām ahaṃ vainān anujānīhi pārthiva
english: "O king, if these men, angry, should restrain me by force — or if I them — permit it, O lord of earth."

sanskrit: etān hi sarvān saṃrabdhān niyantum aham utsahe na tv ahaṃ ninditaṃ karma kuryāṃ pāpaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "I am capable of restraining all of these enraged men; but I would by no means commit a censured, sinful deed."

sanskrit: pāṇḍavārthe hi lubhyantaḥ svārthād dhāsyanti te sutāḥ ete ced evam icchanti kṛtakāryo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: "Craving gain through harming the Pāṇḍavas' cause, your sons will forfeit their own interest. If they desire this, then Yudhiṣṭhira's purpose is already accomplished."

sanskrit: adyaiva hy aham etāṃś ca ye caitān anu bhārata nigṛhya rājan pārthebhyo dadyāṃ kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ bhavet
english: "For this very day I could seize these and all who follow them, O descendant of Bharata, and hand them over to the sons of Pṛthā — what wrong would come of it?"

sanskrit: idaṃ tu na pravarteyaṃ ninditaṃ karma bhārata saṃnidhau te mahārāja krodhajaṃ pāpabuddhijam
english: "But I shall not undertake this censured act, O descendant of Bharata, this act born of anger and evil intention, in your presence, O great king."

sanskrit: eṣa duryodhano rājan yathecchati tathāstu tat ahaṃ tu sarvān samayān anujānāmi bhārata
english: "Let Duryodhana, O king, do as he wishes. But I take leave of all the assembled here, O descendant of Bharata."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu viduraṃ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhyabhāṣata kṣipram ānaya taṃ pāpaṃ rājyalubdhaṃ suyodhanam
english: Hearing this, Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke to Vidura: "Quickly bring that wicked Suyodhana, that one greedy for the kingdom."

sanskrit: sahamitraṃ sahāmātyaṃ sasodaryaṃ sahānugam śaknuyāṃ yadi panthānam avatārayituṃ punaḥ
english: "Along with his allies, ministers, brothers, and followers — if I am able to bring him back onto the right path once more."

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaṃ kṣattā punaḥ prāveśayat sabhām akāmaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ rājabhiḥ parivāritam
english: Then the Kṣattā brought Duryodhana back into the assembly against his will, surrounded by his brothers and the kings.

sanskrit: atha duryodhanaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhyabhāṣata karṇaduḥśāsanābhyāṃ ca rājabhiś cābhisaṃvṛtam
english: Then King Dhṛtarāṣṭra addressed Duryodhana, who was surrounded by Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and the assembled kings.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsa pāpabhūyiṣṭha kṣudrakarmasahāyavān pāpaiḥ sahāyaiḥ saṃhatya pāpaṃ karma cikīrṣasi
english: "O cruel one, O most sinful one, aided by helpers in vile deeds — you conspire with your wicked allies to perpetrate a wicked act."

sanskrit: aśakyam ayaśasyaṃ ca sadbhiś cāpi vigarhitam yathā tvādṛśako mūḍho vyavasyet kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: "An impossible and inglorious deed, condemned even by good men — only such a fool as you, a disgrace to the family, would resolve upon it."

sanskrit: tvam imaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣam apradhṛṣyaṃ durāsadam pāpaiḥ sahāyaiḥ saṃhatya nigrahītuṃ kilecchasi
english: "You, together with your wicked allies, desire to restrain this lotus-eyed one who is unconquerable and unapproachable."

sanskrit: yo na śakyo balātkartuṃ devair api savāsavaiḥ taṃ tvaṃ prārthayase manda bālaś candramasaṃ yathā
english: "You, O dull one, crave to overpower him whom even the gods with Vāsava are unable to constrain by force — as a child might reach for the moon."

sanskrit: devair manuṣyair gandharvair asurair uragaiś ca yaḥ na soḍhuṃ samare śakyas taṃ na budhyasi keśavam
english: "You do not recognize Keśava, whom gods, men, gandharvas, asuras, and serpents together are unable to withstand in battle."

sanskrit: durgrahaḥ pāṇinā vāyur duḥsparśaḥ pāṇinā śaśī durdharā pṛthivī mūrdhnā durgrahaḥ keśavo balāt
english: "Wind cannot be grasped in the hand; the moon cannot be touched by the hand; the earth cannot be held upon the head; and Keśava cannot be seized by force."

sanskrit: ity ukte dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa kṣattāpi viduro 'bravīt duryodhanam abhiprekṣya dhārtarāṣṭram amarṣaṇam
english: When Dhṛtarāṣṭra had spoken thus, the Kṣattā Vidura also spoke, looking at Duryodhana, the impatient son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: saubhadvāre vānarendro dvivido nāma nāmataḥ śilāvarṣeṇa mahatā chādayām āsa keśavam
english: "At the gate of Saubha, the king of monkeys named Dvivida covered Keśava with a mighty shower of rocks —

sanskrit: grahītukāmo vikramya sarvayatnena mādhavam grahītuṃ nāśakat tatra taṃ tvaṃ prārthayase balāt
english: "— desiring to capture him, striving with every effort to seize Mādhava, he could not grasp him there. Yet you seek to seize him by force."

sanskrit: nirmocane ṣaṭ sahasrāḥ pāśair baddhvā mahāsurāḥ grahītuṃ nāśakaṃś cainaṃ taṃ tvaṃ prārthayase balāt
english: "At Nirmochana, six thousand great asuras, having bound him with nooses, could not capture him. Yet you seek to seize him by force."

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣagataṃ śauriṃ narakaḥ saha dānavaiḥ grahītuṃ nāśakat tatra taṃ tvaṃ prārthayase balāt
english: "When Śauri had gone to Prāgjyotiṣa, Naraka together with his danavas could not seize him there. Yet you seek to seize him by force."

sanskrit: anena hi hatā bālye pūtanā śiśunā tathā govardhano dhāritaś ca gavārthe bharatarṣabha
english: "For by this one, even as a child, Putana was slain; and Govardhana was lifted up for the sake of the cows, O bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: ariṣṭo dhenukaś caiva cāṇūraś ca mahābalaḥ aśvarājaś ca nihataḥ kaṃsaś cāriṣṭam ācaran
english: "Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, the mighty Cāṇūra, the king of horses — all were slain, as was Kaṃsa who acted wickedly."

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhaś ca vakraś ca śiśupālaś ca vīryavān bāṇaś ca nihataḥ saṃkhye rājānaś ca niṣūditāḥ
english: "Jarāsandha, Vakra, the valiant Śiśupāla, and Bana were slain in battle, and many kings were destroyed."

sanskrit: varuṇo nirjito rājā pāvakaś cāmitaujasā pārijātaṃ ca haratā jitaḥ sākṣāc chacīpatiḥ
english: "King Varuṇa was vanquished, and Fire was overcome by this one of immeasurable might; even Indra, the lord of Śacī, was conquered when this one carried off the Parijata tree."

sanskrit: ekārṇave śayānena hatau tau madhukaiṭabhau janmāntaram upāgamya hayagrīvas tathā hataḥ
english: "Lying on the cosmic ocean, he slew those two, Madhu and Kaiṭabha; and taking another birth, he slew Hayagrīva likewise."

sanskrit: ayaṃ kartā na kriyate kāraṇaṃ cāpi pauruṣe yad yad icched ayaṃ śauris tat tat kuryād ayatnataḥ
english: "This one acts but is not acted upon; he is the cause behind human effort. Whatever Śauri desires, that he accomplishes without exertion."

sanskrit: taṃ na budhyasi govindaṃ ghoravikramam acyutam āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ tejorāśim anirjitam
english: "You do not recognize Govinda, of terrible valor, the Immovable, that mass of splendor who cannot be conquered — angry like a venomous serpent."

sanskrit: pradharṣayan mahābāhuṃ kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakāriṇam pataṃgo 'gnim ivāsādya sāmātyo na bhaviṣyasi
english: "Attacking the mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, the tireless in action, you and your ministers shall cease to exist, like a moth rushing into fire."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vidureṇaivam ukte tu keśavaḥ śatrupūgahā duryodhanaṃ dhārtarāṣṭram abhyabhāṣata vīryavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When Vidura had spoken thus, the valiant Keśava, the slayer of hosts of enemies, addressed Duryodhana, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: eko 'ham iti yan mohān manyase māṃ suyodhana paribhūya ca durbuddhe grahītuṃ māṃ cikīrṣasi
english: "Through your delusion you think me alone and isolated, O Suyodhana, and with your corrupt mind you desire to seize and humiliate me.

sanskrit: ihaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve tathaivāndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ ihādityāś ca rudrāś ca vasavaś ca maharṣibhiḥ
english: "Right here are all the Pāṇḍavas, and likewise the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis; here too are the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus, together with the great sages."

sanskrit: evam uktvā jahāsoccaiḥ keśavaḥ paravīrahā tasya saṃsmayataḥ śaurer vidyudrūpā mahātmanaḥ aṅguṣṭhamātrās tridaśā mumucuḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Keśava, the slayer of enemy heroes, laughed aloud; and from the body of that great-souled Śauri as he smiled, divine beings of the size of a thumb, shaped like lightning, emitted flames of fire.

sanskrit: tasya brahmā lalāṭastho rudro vakṣasi cābhavat lokapālā bhujeṣv āsann agnir āsyād ajāyata
english: Brahmā appeared on his forehead; Rudra appeared on his chest; the Guardians of the Worlds took their places on his arms; and Fire emerged from his mouth.

sanskrit: ādityāś caiva sādhyāś ca vasavo 'thāśvināv api marutaś ca sahendreṇa viśvedevās tathaiva ca babhūvuś caiva rūpāṇi yakṣagandharvarakṣasām
english: The Ādityas, the Sādhyas, the Vasus, the Aśvins, the Maruts with Indra, the Vishvadevas — all these appeared; and there also appeared the forms of yakshas, gandharvas, and rakshasas.

sanskrit: prādurāstāṃ tathā dorbhyāṃ saṃkarṣaṇadhanaṃjayau dakṣiṇe 'thārjuno dhanvī halī rāmaś ca savyataḥ
english: From his two arms there appeared Saṃkarṣaṇa and Dhanañjaya: on his right was Arjuna with his bow, and on his left was Rāma bearing the plough.

sanskrit: bhīmo yudhiṣṭhiraś caiva mādrīputrau ca pṛṣṭhataḥ andhakā vṛṣṇayaś caiva pradyumnapramukhās tataḥ
english: Bhīma and Yudhiṣṭhira and the two sons of Mādrī appeared behind him; and the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis headed by Pradyumna appeared there as well.

sanskrit: agre babhūvuḥ kṛṣṇasya samudyatamahāyudhāḥ śaṅkhacakragadāśaktiśārṅgalāṅgalanandakāḥ
english: Before Kṛṣṇa appeared his great weapons upraised: the conch, the discus, the mace, the spear, the Śārṅga bow, the plough, and the Nandaka sword.

sanskrit: adṛśyantodyatāny eva sarvapraharaṇāni ca nānābāhuṣu kṛṣṇasya dīpyamānāni sarvaśaḥ
english: And all his weapons were seen upraised, blazing on Kṛṣṇa's many arms in every direction.

sanskrit: netrābhyāṃ nas tataś caiva śrotrābhyāṃ ca samantataḥ prādurāsan mahāraudrāḥ sadhūmāḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ romakūpeṣu ca tathā sūryasyeva marīcayaḥ
english: From his two eyes and his nose and his two ears on all sides there burst forth terrible, smoke-bearing flames of fire; and from his very pores there blazed rays like those of the sun.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā ghoram ātmānaṃ keśavasya mahātmanaḥ nyamīlayanta netrāṇi rājānas trastacetasaḥ
english: Beholding that terrible form of the great-souled Keśava, the kings with terrified minds closed their eyes.

sanskrit: ṛte droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca viduraṃ ca mahāmatim saṃjayaṃ ca mahābhāgam ṛṣīṃś caiva tapodhanān prādāt teṣāṃ sa bhagavān divyaṃ cakṣur janārdanaḥ
english: Except for Droṇa, Bhīṣma, the great-minded Vidura, the illustrious Sañjaya, and the sages rich in austerities — to all of these the blessed Janārdana granted divine sight.

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā mahad āścaryaṃ mādhavasya sabhātale devadundubhayo neduḥ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ca
english: Beholding that great wonder of Mādhava in the hall of the assembly, divine kettledrums sounded and a shower of flowers fell.

sanskrit: cacāla ca mahī kṛtsnā sāgaraś cāpi cukṣubhe vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmuḥ pārthivā bharatarṣabha
english: The whole earth trembled and the ocean was agitated; the kings were filled with utmost wonder, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghraḥ saṃjahāra vapuḥ svakam tāṃ divyām adbhutāṃ citrām ṛddhimattām ariṃdamaḥ
english: Then that tiger among men, that subduer of enemies, withdrew his own divine, wondrous, brilliant, and glorious form.

sanskrit: tataḥ sātyakim ādāya pāṇau hārdikyam eva ca ṛṣibhis tair anujñāto niryayau madhusūdanaḥ
english: Then, taking Sātyaki and Hārdikya by the hand, and being permitted to depart by those sages, the Madhusūdana went forth.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo 'ntarhitā jagmus tatas te nāradādayaḥ tasmin kolāhale vṛtte tad adbhutam abhūt tadā
english: Then those sages, Nārada and the others, vanished from sight and departed; and amidst that tumult, a wondrous thing came to pass.

sanskrit: taṃ prasthitam abhiprekṣya kauravāḥ saha rājabhiḥ anujagmur naravyāghraṃ devā iva śatakratum
english: Beholding him setting out, the Kauravas together with the assembled kings followed that tiger among men, as gods follow the hundred-sacrificed Indra.

sanskrit: acintayann ameyātmā sarvaṃ tad rājamaṇḍalam niścakrāma tataḥ śauriḥ sadhūma iva pāvakaḥ
english: Giving no thought to all that assemblage of kings, the immeasurable-souled Śauri then went forth like a fire with its smoke.

sanskrit: tato rathena śubhreṇa mahatā kiṅkiṇīkinā hemajālavicitreṇa laghunā meghanādinā
english: Then with a bright, great chariot adorned with bells, decorated with nets of gold, swift and thundering like a cloud —

sanskrit: sūpaskareṇa śubhreṇa vaiyāghreṇa varūthinā sainyasugrīvayuktena pratyadṛśyata dārukaḥ
english: — well-equipped and bright, covered with tiger-skins for its canopy, yoked with Sainya and Sugrīva — there appeared Dāruka the charioteer.

sanskrit: tathaiva ratham āsthāya kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ vṛṣṇīnāṃ saṃmato vīro hārdikyaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Likewise, mounting his chariot, the great chariot-warrior Kṛtavarman, the hero honored by the Vṛṣṇis, the son of Hridika, also appeared.

sanskrit: upasthitarathaṃ śauriṃ prayāsyantam ariṃdamam dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājaḥ punar evābhyabhāṣata
english: As Śauri, the subduer of enemies, stood ready at his chariot about to depart, the great king Dhṛtarāṣṭra spoke to him once more.

sanskrit: yāvad balaṃ me putreṣu paśyasy etaj janārdana pratyakṣaṃ te na te kiṃ cit parokṣaṃ śatrukarśana
english: "O Janārdana, you see this much power in my sons directly before you — nothing is hidden from you, O afflicterof enemies."

sanskrit: kurūṇāṃ śamam icchantaṃ yatamānaṃ ca keśava viditvaitām avasthāṃ me nātiśaṅkitum arhasi
english: "Knowing me to be one who desires peace for the Kurus and is striving for it, O Keśava, you should not harbor excessive suspicion of me."

sanskrit: na me pāpo 'sty abhiprāyaḥ pāṇḍavān prati keśava jñātam eva hi te vākyaṃ yan mayoktaḥ suyodhanaḥ
english: "I have no wicked intention toward the Pāṇḍavas, O Keśava; you already know the words with which I addressed Suyodhana."

sanskrit: jānanti kuravaḥ sarve rājānaś caiva pārthivāḥ śame prayatamānaṃ māṃ sarvayatnena mādhava
english: "All the Kurus know, as do the assembled kings and lords of earth, that I have been striving for peace with every effort, O Mādhava."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahābāhur dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram droṇaṃ pitāmahaṃ bhīṣmaṃ kṣattāraṃ bāhlikaṃ kṛpam
english: Then the mighty-armed one spoke to Dhṛtarāṣṭra the lord of men, to Droṇa, the grandsire Bhīṣma, the Kṣattā, Bahlika, and Kṛpa:

sanskrit: pratyakṣam etad bhavatāṃ yad vṛttaṃ kurusaṃsadi yathā cāśiṣṭavan mando roṣād asakṛd utthitaḥ
english: "What has transpired in this assembly of the Kurus is evident to you all — how this dull one, ill-mannered, has repeatedly risen up in anger."
